pages.title: Writing Books
pages.markdown:
# Writing Books

A folder directly under `docs/` becomes a book. Each Markdown file in that book is a chapter.

```text
docs/
├── field-notes/
│   ├── index.md
│   └── 01-setup.md
└── release-notes/
    ├── index.md
    ├── v1.4.md
    └── v1.5.md
```

Files directly in `docs/` share a book of their own. The bookshelf opens when the project has book folders.

pages.title: Writing Books
pages.markdown:
## Chapters and sections

Inside a book, `index.md` comes first. Other chapters follow in filename order, including files in subfolders. For a series such as release notes, keep separate version files in the same folder.

Use H1 for the chapter title. An H2 opens a new page. When the first H2 immediately follows the chapter title, they share the first page. Use H3 for subheadings within a page. The table of contents groups H2 sections and their page numbers under each chapter.

pages.title: Writing Books
pages.markdown:
## Titles, links, and covers

The H1 in the book's `index.md` names the book. Keep your paths in English and write titles in your readers' language. Set `locale: ja` in `grimoire.yml` to display the reader controls in Japanese.

Link to other chapters with relative Markdown paths and an optional heading anchor. For example, `[Drawings](./media.md#mermaid-diagrams)` opens [the Mermaid section](./media.md#mermaid-diagrams). You can also copy a chapter or section URL directly from the reader.

Set the cover in the book's `index.md` front matter. Available covers are `red`, `green`, `blue`, `plum`, `amber`, `teal`, `black`, `ivory`, `walnut`, and `slate`. Books without a cover setting use a color based on their folder path.

```markdown
---
cover: teal
---
# Release Notes
```

pages.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
pages.markdown:
# Formatting and Spell Mode

Grimoire3D renders headings, lists, block quotes, links, **bold**, *italics*, ~~strikethrough~~, and `inline code`. Use a fenced code block for commands or snippets.

pages.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
pages.markdown:
## Paper marks

:underline[Underline a term], :highlight[highlight a phrase], or call something out in :red[red ink].

```markdown
:underline[Underline a term]
:highlight[highlight a phrase]
:red[red ink]
```

> [!WARNING]
> Keep a copy of your Markdown and media when moving an existing library.

Start a block quote with `[!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]`, or `[!CAUTION]` to create a callout.

pages.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
pages.markdown:
## Tables and matrices

Use GitHub Flavored Markdown table syntax. On a narrow page, the table scrolls horizontally and its first column stays visible for comparison.

| Format | Live preview | Static site | Inline control | Interaction | Content source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AVIF | Yes | Yes | Image | Read | Local or remote |
| GIF | Yes | Yes | Image | Animate | Local or remote |
| MP4 | Yes | Yes | Video | Play and seek | Local or remote |
| Mermaid | Yes | Yes | Diagram | Zoom and pan | Markdown fence |

pages.title: Formatting and Spell Mode
pages.markdown:
## Spell Mode

Set `magicMode: true` in `grimoire.yml` to add a **Spell mode** toggle to the reader. After a page comes to rest, the marker draws a stroke that stays on the paper, bold letters lift and settle, and strikethrough draws across the words.

The effects play once each time the page comes into view, or when you enable Spell mode on an open page. The reader respects the device's reduced-motion setting.

pages.title: Images, video, and diagrams
pages.markdown:
# Images, video, and diagrams

Use Markdown image syntax for still images, animated GIFs, and MP4 files. Resolve local paths from the chapter that uses them. The static build bundles referenced local media.

pages.title: Images, video, and diagrams
pages.markdown:
## Images and GIFs

Use AVIF, WebP, PNG, JPEG, or GIF. Write an alt description inside the brackets.

```markdown
![From Markdown to a static site](../assets/diagram.avif)
![The publishing flow in motion](../assets/publishing-flow.gif)
```

![From Markdown to a static site](../assets/diagram.avif)

![The publishing flow in motion](../assets/publishing-flow.gif)

pages.title: Images, video, and diagrams
pages.markdown:
## MP4

An MP4 renders as a video player inside the page. Playback pauses when you turn away from it.

```markdown
![Publishing flow video](../assets/publishing-flow.mp4)
```

![Publishing flow video](../assets/publishing-flow.mp4)

pages.title: Images, video, and diagrams
pages.markdown:
## YouTube and Vimeo

Use the video URL in the same syntax. The embedded player loads when the reader selects it. The source link still works when the video owner restricts embedding.

```markdown
![YouTube demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M7lc1UVf-VE)
![Vimeo demo](https://vimeo.com/76979871)
```

![YouTube demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M7lc1UVf-VE)

pages.title: Images, video, and diagrams
pages.markdown:
## Mermaid diagrams

Set the language of a fenced code block to `mermaid`. Select the diagram to open the viewer, then zoom and drag to explore. You can also pan with the arrow keys and press Escape to return to the page.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Source
    Markdown[Markdown chapters]
    Settings[Project settings]
    Art[Images and video]
  end
  subgraph Build
    Books[Sort books and chapters]
    Paper[Split pages at H2]
    Links[Resolve links and media]
  end
  subgraph Output
    Library[Library]
    Chapters[Chapter HTML]
    Sitemap[Sitemap]
  end
  Markdown --> Books --> Paper --> Chapters
  Art --> Links --> Chapters
  Settings --> Library
  Settings --> Sitemap
  Books --> Library
```
